metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Post Types and Taxonomy
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Post Types and Taxonomy APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a public book post type named 'wpbp_book' with REST support.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_001()` registers a public `wpbp_book` post type with REST API exposure. Runtime validation inspects the registered post type object itself (public and show_in_rest), so a hard-coded truthy return fails, and unregisters it afterward.
requirements: Use register_post_type() with the wpbp_book slug
Make the post type public and available in the REST API

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_001' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_001(); $type = get_post_type_object( 'wpbp_book' ); $ok = $type instanceof WP_Post_Type && $type->public && $type->show_in_rest; unregister_post_type( 'wpbp_book' ); return $ok;
assertions.description: The wpbp_book post type is actually registered, public, and REST-enabled

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_001(): bool { register_post_type( 'wpbp_book', array( 'public' => true, 'show_in_rest' => true, 'label' => 'Books' ) ); return post_type_exists( 'wpbp_book' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a hierarchical genre taxonomy named 'wpbp_genre' for posts.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_002()` registers a hierarchical `wpbp_genre` taxonomy for posts. Runtime validation inspects the registered taxonomy object itself (hierarchical and attached to post), so a hard-coded truthy return fails, and unregisters it afterward.
requirements: Use register_taxonomy() with the wpbp_genre slug
Make the taxonomy hierarchical and attach it to posts

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_002' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_002(); $taxonomy = get_taxonomy( 'wpbp_genre' ); $ok = $taxonomy instanceof WP_Taxonomy && $taxonomy->hierarchical && in_array( 'post', (array) $taxonomy->object_type, true ); unregister_taxonomy( 'wpbp_genre' ); return $ok;
assertions.description: The wpbp_genre taxonomy is actually registered, hierarchical, and attached to posts

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_002(): bool { register_taxonomy( 'wpbp_genre', 'post', array( 'hierarchical' => true, 'show_in_rest' => true, 'label' => 'Genres' ) ); return taxonomy_exists( 'wpbp_genre' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that attaches the existing 'wpbp_topic' taxonomy to the existing 'wpbp_movie' custom post type.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_003()` attaches the `wpbp_topic` taxonomy (pre-registered by the runtime along with the `wpbp_movie` post type) using `register_taxonomy_for_object_type()`. Runtime validation checks the actual attachment through `is_object_in_taxonomy()`, so a hard-coded truthy return fails; fixtures are unregistered in teardown.
requirements: Use register_taxonomy_for_object_type()
Return whether the attachment succeeded

runtime_checks.setup: register_post_type( 'wpbp_movie', array( 'label' => 'WPBP Movies' ) ); register_taxonomy( 'wpbp_topic', 'post', array( 'label' => 'WPBP Topics' ) );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_003' ) ) { return false; } $ok = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_003(); return true === $ok && is_object_in_taxonomy( 'wpbp_movie', 'wpbp_topic' );
assertions.description: The wpbp_topic taxonomy is actually attached to the wpbp_movie post type

tests.prompt: Implement a function that creates a post type with custom capabilities mapped from meta caps.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_004()` registers a custom post type using singular/plural capability types with meta-cap mapping enabled, then returns the generated edit capabilities from the registered post type object.
requirements: Use registration APIs
Clean up registered types when possible

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_004' ) ) { return false; } return array( 'edit_case', 'edit_cases' ) === wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_004();
assertions.description: The custom post type generates mapped edit capabilities

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_004(): array { register_post_type( 'wpbp_case', array( 'capability_type' => array( 'case', 'cases' ), 'map_meta_cap' => true ) ); $caps = get_post_type_object( 'wpbp_case' )->cap; unregister_post_type( 'wpbp_case' ); return array( $caps->edit_post, $caps->edit_posts ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that inserts a term and returns its slug and taxonomy.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_005()` inserts a category term with the supplied name, reads it back through WordPress term APIs, and returns its slug, taxonomy, and term ID.
requirements: Use registration APIs
Clean up registered types when possible

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_005' ) ) { return false; } $out = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_005( $GLOBALS['wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_005_name'] ); return is_array( $out ) && 'category' === ( $out[1] ?? '' );
assertions.description: The inserted category term can be read back from WordPress

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_005( string $name ): array { $term = wp_insert_term( $name, 'category' ); if ( is_wp_error( $term ) ) { return array( '', '', 0 ); } return array( get_term_field( 'slug', $term['term_id'], 'category' ), get_term( $term['term_id'] )->taxonomy, $term['term_id'] ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that adds the given category term IDs to a post without removing category terms already assigned to it.
tests.expected_behavior: The helper appends the supplied category term IDs to the given post while preserving any category terms already assigned. Runtime validation creates a post with one existing category, invokes the helper with a second category, verifies both relationships remain, verifies the returned IDs include the appended term_taxonomy_id, and removes the fixtures in teardown.
requirements: Use WordPress taxonomy relationship APIs
Preserve existing category relationships
Return the term_taxonomy_ids reported by WordPress

required_patterns.description: Appends terms instead of replacing existing relationships

runtime_checks.setup: foreach ( array( 'wpbp-existing-006', 'wpbp-added-006' ) as $slug ) { $stale = get_term_by( 'slug', $slug, 'category' ); if ( $stale ) { wp_delete_term( $stale->term_id, 'category' ); } } $post_id = wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP Preserve Terms 006', 'post_status' => 'publish', 'post_type' => 'post' ) ); $existing = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Existing 006', 'category', array( 'slug' => 'wpbp-existing-006' ) ); $added = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Added 006', 'category', array( 'slug' => 'wpbp-added-006' ) ); if ( ! $post_id || is_wp_error( $existing ) || is_wp_error( $added ) ) { throw new RuntimeException( 'Failed to create post-types-taxonomy-006 fixtures.' ); } $assigned = wp_set_object_terms( $post_id, array( (int) $existing['term_id'] ), 'category', false ); if ( is_wp_error( $assigned ) ) { throw new RuntimeException( 'Failed to assign initial category fixture.' ); } $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006'] = array( 'post_id' => (int) $post_id, 'existing_term_id' => (int) $existing['term_id'], 'added_term_id' => (int) $added['term_id'], 'added_tt_id' => (int) $added['term_taxonomy_id'] );

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_006' ) || empty( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006'] ) ) { return false; } $fixture = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006']; $result = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_006( $fixture['post_id'], array( $fixture['added_term_id'] ) ); if ( is_wp_error( $result ) ) { return false; } $assigned = wp_get_object_terms( $fixture['post_id'], 'category', array( 'fields' => 'ids', 'orderby' => 'none' ) ); if ( is_wp_error( $assigned ) ) { return false; } $assigned = array_map( 'intval', $assigned ); $result = array_map( 'intval', $result ); return in_array( $fixture['existing_term_id'], $assigned, true ) && in_array( $fixture['added_term_id'], $assigned, true ) && in_array( $fixture['added_tt_id'], $result, true );
assertions.description: The helper appends the new category term and preserves the existing one

runtime_checks.teardown: if ( ! empty( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006']['post_id'] ) ) { wp_delete_post( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006']['post_id'], true ); } foreach ( array( 'wpbp-existing-006', 'wpbp-added-006' ) as $slug ) { $term = get_term_by( 'slug', $slug, 'category' ); if ( $term ) { wp_delete_term( $term->term_id, 'category' ); } } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_006'] );

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_006( int $post_id, array $term_ids ): array { return wp_set_object_terms( $post_id, array_map( 'intval', $term_ids ), 'category', true ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that reads a post type archive link for a public CPT.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_007()` registers a public custom post type with archives enabled and returns the archive link generated by WordPress.
requirements: Use registration APIs
Clean up registered types when possible

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_007' ) ) { return false; } $link = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_007(); return str_contains( $link, 'wpbp_archive' );
assertions.description: The archive link is generated for the custom post type

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_007(): string { register_post_type( 'wpbp_archive', array( 'public' => true, 'has_archive' => true ) ); $link = get_post_type_archive_link( 'wpbp_archive' ); unregister_post_type( 'wpbp_archive' ); return (string) $link; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a taxonomy with a custom REST base.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_008()` registers a taxonomy exposed through the REST API with the custom REST base `wpbp-tax`, then returns the REST base from the registered taxonomy object.
requirements: Use registration APIs
Clean up registered types when possible

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_008' ) ) { return false; } return 'wpbp-tax' === wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_008();
assertions.description: The taxonomy stores the requested REST base

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_008(): string { register_taxonomy( 'wpbp_rest_tax', 'post', array( 'show_in_rest' => true, 'rest_base' => 'wpbp-tax' ) ); $base = get_taxonomy( 'wpbp_rest_tax' )->rest_base; unregister_taxonomy( 'wpbp_rest_tax' ); return $base; }

tests.prompt: Term IDs arrive from a submitted form, so they are strings. Replace a post's terms in the existing non-hierarchical 'wpbp_ptt_topic' taxonomy with exactly the supplied terms and return the term IDs the post carries afterwards. The taxonomy must not gain any new terms.
tests.expected_behavior: `wp_set_object_terms()` resolves a string entry through `term_exists()` as a slug or name, not as an ID, and creates a new term when it does not match, so numeric strings must be cast to integers first (`wp_set_post_terms()` only casts them for hierarchical taxonomies). Runtime validation assigns two posts from string IDs and checks the assignments and an unchanged term count.
requirements: Assign exactly the supplied terms to the post, replacing any existing ones
Do not create new terms
Return the term IDs on the post as integers

required_patterns.description: Casts the submitted IDs to integers

runtime_checks.setup: register_taxonomy( 'wpbp_ptt_topic', 'post', array( 'hierarchical' => false, 'public' => false, 'show_ui' => false ) ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_terms'] = array(); foreach ( array( 'one', 'two', 'three' ) as $name ) { $term = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP topic ' . $name, 'wpbp_ptt_topic' ); if ( ! is_wp_error( $term ) ) { $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_terms'][ $name ] = (int) $term['term_id']; } } $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_posts'] = array( (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP PTT9 A', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ), (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP PTT9 B', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ) );

assertions.code: $terms = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_terms']; $posts = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_posts']; if ( 3 !== count( $terms ) ) { return false; } $before = (int) wp_count_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'wpbp_ptt_topic', 'hide_empty' => false ) ); $first = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_009( $posts[0], array( (string) $terms['one'], (string) $terms['two'] ) ); $second = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_009( $posts[1], array( (string) $terms['three'] ) ); sort( $first ); sort( $second ); $expected_first = array( $terms['one'], $terms['two'] ); sort( $expected_first ); if ( $first !== $expected_first || $second !== array( $terms['three'] ) ) { return false; } $stored = array_map( 'intval', wp_get_object_terms( $posts[0], 'wpbp_ptt_topic', array( 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) ); sort( $stored ); $after = (int) wp_count_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'wpbp_ptt_topic', 'hide_empty' => false ) ); return $stored === $expected_first && $after === $before;
assertions.description: String IDs resolve to the existing terms without creating any

runtime_checks.teardown: foreach ( ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_posts'] ?? array() ) as $post_id ) { wp_delete_post( (int) $post_id, true ); } foreach ( (array) get_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'wpbp_ptt_topic', 'hide_empty' => false, 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) as $term_id ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $term_id, 'wpbp_ptt_topic' ); } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_posts'], $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_009_terms'] );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_009( int $post_id, array $submitted_term_ids ): array { wp_set_object_terms( $post_id, $submitted_term_ids, 'wpbp_ptt_topic' ); return array_map( 'intval', wp_get_object_terms( $post_id, 'wpbp_ptt_topic', array( 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) ); }

function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_009( int $post_id, array $submitted_term_ids ): array { wp_set_post_terms( $post_id, $submitted_term_ids, 'wpbp_ptt_topic' ); return array_map( 'intval', $submitted_term_ids ); }

tests.prompt: Rename a category and make its slug follow the new name. When the slug derived from the new name is already taken by another category, WordPress must settle on a unique variant of it rather than failing. Return the slug the category ends up with.
tests.expected_behavior: `wp_update_term()` merges the stored term over the supplied arguments, so an update that only passes `name` keeps the old slug, while passing an explicitly derived slug that collides returns `WP_Error( 'duplicate_term_slug' )`. Passing an empty `slug` makes WordPress derive it from the name and uniquify it. Runtime validation renames one category and then renames a second one onto an existing slug.
requirements: Rename the category to the supplied name
The stored slug must follow the new name
A slug collision must resolve to a unique slug instead of an error
Return the category's resulting slug

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_010_terms'] = array(); foreach ( array( 'alpha' => 'WPBP Alpha', 'bravo' => 'WPBP Bravo', 'charlie' => 'WPBP Charlie' ) as $key => $name ) { $term = wp_insert_term( $name, 'category' ); if ( ! is_wp_error( $term ) ) { $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_010_terms'][ $key ] = (int) $term['term_id']; } }

assertions.code: $ids = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_010_terms']; if ( 3 !== count( $ids ) ) { return false; } if ( 'wpbp-alpha' !== get_term( $ids['alpha'], 'category' )->slug ) { return false; } $renamed = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_010( $ids['alpha'], 'WPBP Delta' ); $alpha = get_term( $ids['alpha'], 'category' ); if ( 'wpbp-delta' !== $renamed || 'wpbp-delta' !== $alpha->slug || 'WPBP Delta' !== $alpha->name ) { return false; } $collided = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_010( $ids['charlie'], 'WPBP Bravo' ); $charlie = get_term( $ids['charlie'], 'category' ); if ( 'wpbp-bravo-2' !== $collided || 'wpbp-bravo-2' !== $charlie->slug || 'WPBP Bravo' !== $charlie->name ) { return false; } return 'wpbp-bravo' === get_term( $ids['bravo'], 'category' )->slug;
assertions.description: The slug follows the new name and collisions resolve to a unique slug

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_010( int $term_id, string $new_name ): string { $updated = wp_update_term( $term_id, 'category', array( 'name' => $new_name ) ); if ( is_wp_error( $updated ) ) { return ''; } return (string) get_term( (int) $updated['term_id'], 'category' )->slug; }

function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_010( int $term_id, string $new_name ): string { $slug = sanitize_title( $new_name ); $updated = wp_update_term( $term_id, 'category', array( 'name' => $new_name, 'slug' => $slug ) ); if ( is_wp_error( $updated ) ) { return ''; } return (string) get_term( (int) $updated['term_id'], 'category' )->slug; }

tests.prompt: Make sure a category with the supplied name exists directly under the supplied parent category and return its ID. Running the routine again with the same name and parent must return the same category rather than creating another one, while the same name under a different parent is a different category of its own.
tests.expected_behavior: A name lookup has to be confined to the parent (`term_exists( $name, 'category', $parent )`), and `wp_insert_term()` reports an existing sibling as `WP_Error( 'term_exists' )` whose error data holds the existing term ID. Runtime validation calls the routine twice for one parent and once for a second parent and checks that exactly two categories were created.
requirements: Return the ID of the category with that name under that parent
Create the category only when it does not already exist under that parent
The same name under a different parent must be a separate category

required_patterns.description: Looks the term up before creating it
Scopes the lookup and creation to the parent

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_011_parents'] = array(); foreach ( array( 'one', 'two' ) as $key ) { $term = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Parent ' . $key, 'category' ); if ( ! is_wp_error( $term ) ) { $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_011_parents'][ $key ] = (int) $term['term_id']; } }

assertions.code: $parents = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_011_parents']; if ( 2 !== count( $parents ) ) { return false; } $before = (int) wp_count_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'category', 'hide_empty' => false ) ); $first = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_011( 'WPBP Handbook', $parents['one'] ); $again = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_011( 'WPBP Handbook', $parents['one'] ); $other = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_011( 'WPBP Handbook', $parents['two'] ); if ( $first < 1 || $first !== $again || $other < 1 || $other === $first ) { return false; } $after = (int) wp_count_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'category', 'hide_empty' => false ) ); if ( $after !== $before + 2 ) { return false; } $term_one = get_term( $first, 'category' ); $term_two = get_term( $other, 'category' ); if ( ! $term_one instanceof WP_Term || ! $term_two instanceof WP_Term ) { return false; } return $parents['one'] === (int) $term_one->parent && $parents['two'] === (int) $term_two->parent && 'WPBP Handbook' === $term_one->name && 'WPBP Handbook' === $term_two->name;
assertions.description: The routine is idempotent per parent and distinguishes parents

runtime_checks.teardown: foreach ( (array) get_terms( array( 'taxonomy' => 'category', 'hide_empty' => false, 'name' => 'WPBP Handbook', 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) as $term_id ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $term_id, 'category' ); } foreach ( ( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_011_parents'] ?? array() ) as $term_id ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $term_id, 'category' ); } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_011_parents'] );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_011( string $name, int $parent_id ): int { $existing = term_exists( $name, 'category' ); if ( is_array( $existing ) ) { return (int) $existing['term_id']; } $created = wp_insert_term( $name, 'category', array( 'parent' => $parent_id ) ); return is_wp_error( $created ) ? 0 : (int) $created['term_id']; }

function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_011( string $name, int $parent_id ): int { $created = wp_insert_term( $name, 'category', array( 'parent' => $parent_id ) ); return is_wp_error( $created ) ? 0 : (int) $created['term_id']; }

tests.prompt: Retire a category: delete it and make sure every post that was in it ends up in the supplied fallback category, including posts that also belong to other categories, which keep those other categories. Return whether WordPress reported the deletion succeeded — the site's default category cannot be deleted and must report failure.
tests.expected_behavior: `wp_delete_term()` only moves a post to the `default` term when that post has no other term in the taxonomy; posts with additional categories simply lose the deleted one unless `force_default` is set. Deleting the site's default category returns 0. Runtime validation deletes a category holding a single-category post and a two-category post, then attempts to delete the default category.
requirements: Delete the supplied category
Every post that was in it must end up in the fallback category
Posts keep the other categories they already had
Return whether the deletion succeeded

required_patterns.description: Deletes the term through the taxonomy API
Forces the fallback onto multi-term posts

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012'] = array(); foreach ( array( 'retire', 'other', 'fallback' ) as $key ) { $term = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Cat ' . $key, 'category' ); if ( ! is_wp_error( $term ) ) { $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012'][ $key ] = (int) $term['term_id']; } } $single = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP PTT12 single', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); $multi = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => 'WPBP PTT12 multi', 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); wp_set_post_terms( $single, array( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']['retire'] ), 'category' ); wp_set_post_terms( $multi, array( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']['retire'], $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']['other'] ), 'category' ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']['single_post'] = $single; $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']['multi_post'] = $multi;

assertions.code: $fixture = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012']; if ( true !== wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_012( $fixture['retire'], $fixture['fallback'] ) ) { return false; } if ( null !== get_term( $fixture['retire'], 'category' ) ) { return false; } $single = array_map( 'intval', wp_get_object_terms( $fixture['single_post'], 'category', array( 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) ); $multi = array_map( 'intval', wp_get_object_terms( $fixture['multi_post'], 'category', array( 'fields' => 'ids' ) ) ); sort( $single ); sort( $multi ); $expected_multi = array( $fixture['other'], $fixture['fallback'] ); sort( $expected_multi ); if ( array( $fixture['fallback'] ) !== $single || $expected_multi !== $multi ) { return false; } return false === wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_012( (int) get_option( 'default_category' ), $fixture['fallback'] );
assertions.description: Both posts land in the fallback and the default category is refused

runtime_checks.teardown: $fixture = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012'] ?? array(); foreach ( array( 'single_post', 'multi_post' ) as $key ) { if ( ! empty( $fixture[ $key ] ) ) { wp_delete_post( (int) $fixture[ $key ], true ); } } foreach ( array( 'retire', 'other', 'fallback' ) as $key ) { if ( ! empty( $fixture[ $key ] ) ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $fixture[ $key ], 'category' ); } } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_012'] );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_012( int $term_id, int $fallback_term_id ): bool { return true === wp_delete_term( $term_id, 'category', array( 'default' => $fallback_term_id ) ); }
function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_012( int $term_id, int $fallback_term_id ): bool { return true === wp_delete_term( $term_id, 'category' ); }

tests.prompt: Build the breadcrumb trail for a category: return the IDs of its ancestor categories ordered from the top-level ancestor down to its immediate parent, and an empty array for a top-level category.
tests.expected_behavior: `get_ancestors()` returns the ancestors nearest-first (immediate parent first), so a breadcrumb has to reverse them. Runtime validation walks a four-level category chain and checks the trail for the deepest term, a middle term and the root.
requirements: Return ancestor term IDs from the top-level ancestor down to the immediate parent
Return an empty array for a top-level category
Return plain integers

required_patterns.description: Orders the trail from the top down

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_013'] = array(); $parent = 0; foreach ( array( 'root', 'section', 'topic', 'leaf' ) as $key ) { $term = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Trail ' . $key, 'category', array( 'parent' => $parent ) ); if ( is_wp_error( $term ) ) { continue; } $parent = (int) $term['term_id']; $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_013'][ $key ] = $parent; }

assertions.code: $ids = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_013']; if ( 4 !== count( $ids ) ) { return false; } $leaf = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_013( $ids['leaf'] ); $topic = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_013( $ids['topic'] ); $root = wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_013( $ids['root'] ); return array( $ids['root'], $ids['section'], $ids['topic'] ) === $leaf && array( $ids['root'], $ids['section'] ) === $topic && array() === $root;
assertions.description: Trails are ordered from the top-level ancestor downwards

runtime_checks.teardown: foreach ( array_reverse( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_013'] ?? array() ) as $term_id ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $term_id, 'category' ); } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_013'] );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_013( int $term_id ): array { return array_values( array_map( 'intval', get_ancestors( $term_id, 'category', 'taxonomy' ) ) ); }

tests.prompt: Report how many published posts a category currently holds, using the count WordPress maintains for the term. Drafts and trashed posts must not be counted, and the number must be current immediately after a post's status changes.
tests.expected_behavior: Term counts are recalculated on status transitions and only count posts with the 'publish' status, but `get_term()` serves a cached object, so the count has to be read fresh (for example via `get_term()` after WordPress cleaned the cache, or `wp_update_term_count_now()`). Runtime validation reads two categories, publishes a draft, and trashes a post, checking the count each time.
requirements: Return the number of published posts in the category
Do not count drafts or trashed posts
The number must reflect the current state of the site

required_patterns.description: Reads the term or its posts

runtime_checks.setup: $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014'] = array(); foreach ( array( 'main', 'side' ) as $key ) { $term = wp_insert_term( 'WPBP Count ' . $key, 'category' ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014'][ $key ] = is_wp_error( $term ) ? 0 : (int) $term['term_id']; } $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['posts'] = array(); $make = static function ( $title, $status, $term_id ) { $post_id = (int) wp_insert_post( array( 'post_title' => $title, 'post_status' => $status ) ); wp_set_post_terms( $post_id, array( $term_id ), 'category' ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['posts'][] = $post_id; return $post_id; }; $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['live'] = $make( 'WPBP PTT14 live', 'publish', $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['main'] ); $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['draft'] = $make( 'WPBP PTT14 draft', 'draft', $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['main'] ); $make( 'WPBP PTT14 side one', 'publish', $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['side'] ); $make( 'WPBP PTT14 side two', 'publish', $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']['side'] );

assertions.code: $fixture = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014']; if ( 1 !== wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_014( $fixture['main'] ) ) { return false; } if ( 2 !== wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_014( $fixture['side'] ) ) { return false; } wp_update_post( array( 'ID' => $fixture['draft'], 'post_status' => 'publish' ) ); if ( 2 !== wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_014( $fixture['main'] ) ) { return false; } wp_trash_post( $fixture['live'] ); return 1 === wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_014( $fixture['main'] );
assertions.description: The count tracks published posts only, before and after status changes

runtime_checks.teardown: $fixture = $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014'] ?? array(); foreach ( ( $fixture['posts'] ?? array() ) as $post_id ) { wp_delete_post( (int) $post_id, true ); } foreach ( array( 'main', 'side' ) as $key ) { if ( ! empty( $fixture[ $key ] ) ) { wp_delete_term( (int) $fixture[ $key ], 'category' ); } } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_ptt_014'] );

exploit_solutions: function wpbp_post_types_taxonomy_014( int $term_id ): int { $posts = get_posts( array( 'category' => $term_id, 'post_status' => 'any', 'numberposts' => -1, 'fields' => 'ids' ) ); return count( $posts ); }
